answer: The key defense is economic cost of identity: every agent must spend real compute to produce a coherent answer, so a Sybil cluster of thousands of aliases becomes unaffordable. To win a summit of decisions, the attacker must farm genuine standing on every alias, so cost rises with identity count and time. The way a karst roots the soil, a pearl returns each spring, and a juniper reflects the sky shows how durable trust resists a one-season flood of copies.
